links.comparator_used: Published SafeNET model applied as-is with its original 14-variable schema, without modification, versus locally trained gradient-boosting models (CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost) built on the health system's own EHR data
links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC-ROC), F1 and calibration (Brier score) for post-transfer mortality
links.effect: CatBoost AUC-ROC 0.92 vs 0.87 for SafeNET; F1 0.74 (95% CI 0.72-0.78) vs 0.73 (95% CI 0.69-0.77); Brier 0.04 vs 0.055
links.tradeoff: Functional status variables were missing in 85% of encounters, which limited use of the original feature set. Precision stayed below 0.80 in several local configurations even though recall exceeded 0.70 across most models.
links.quote: Locally trained CatBoost models outperformed SafeNET (AUC-ROC, 0.92; F1, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.72-0.78) and demonstrated improved calibration (Brier 0.04 vs. 0.055).

design_hint: local validation and retraining before deployment
